css:
/* THE ARROW MUST SIT AT THE SAME HEIGHT IN EVERY REACTION.
   `display:none` on an empty label made the grid asymmetric about
   the arrow row, so `vertical-align:middle` centred a different
   box each time. Measured at 19px: the arrow sat 1px below the
   text baseline with a top label only, 9px with both, and 18px
   with a bottom label only — a 17px swing, so in one answer no
   two arrows lined up with each other or with the species either
   side of them. That is what read as reactions not being on one
   line.
   An empty label now KEEPS its row at the label's own height, so
   the grid is always three symmetric rows and the arrow is always
   the middle one. */
.rxn>.rxn-t, .rxn>.rxn-b { min-height:1.16em; }
.rxn>.rxn-t:empty, .rxn>.rxn-b:empty { min-height:1.16em; }

/* AN ATOM STAYS ON THE BASELINE; ITS LABELS HANG OFF IT.
   This is the rule that makes a structure a structure.
   The source numbers a chain as
   `\overset{3}{CH_3}-\overset{2}{CH}-\overset{1}{CH_2}-Br` — 52 of
   them — and the bond dashes between the atoms are ordinary text
   sitting on the text baseline. An inline-grid takes its baseline
   from its FIRST row, so with the number in row 1 the grid aligned
   the NUMBER to the baseline and pushed every atom below it: the
   dashes ran between the numbers instead of between the carbons,
   the atoms looked detached, and a substituent's vertical bond met
   nothing.
   So the atom is row 1 — the grid's baseline row, level with the
   dashes either side of it — and a number or charge is positioned
   ABSOLUTELY above it. Absolute because a carbon number must not
   take part in layout at all: it is anchored to its own atom and
   cannot be moved independently of it, which is exactly the
   complaint. A name below stays in flow, because a name is wide
   and does need its width reserved. */
.sp { display:inline-grid; grid-template-rows:auto auto;
      justify-items:center; position:relative; white-space:nowrap;
      vertical-align:baseline; margin:0 1px; }
.sp>.sp-c { grid-row:1; white-space:nowrap; }
